description:
Somebody else in this market: a competitor, a supplier, a buyer, a partner, or a farm somebody is thinking about buying. One record per organisation, and the type is a column rather than five doctypes because the same grower is a competitor for labour, a partner in a packing shed and a possible acquisition in the same season, and splitting them would make that one organisation three records that drift apart.

THE ESTIMATES ARE LABELLED AS ESTIMATES AND THAT IS THE POINT. Revenue, acreage and market share here are somebody's read of a private business, not filed accounts. They are worth writing down — a competitor's acreage is what decides whether a price move matters — and they are worth never confusing with the numbers in the ledger, which is why every one of them says `estimated` in its own name.

fields.description: The organisation's name as it is actually known locally, not its filing name.
fields.label: Participant Name

fields.description: What this organisation is TO US. One participant can be several things at once; record the one that drives the decisions being made about them now, and say the rest in the notes.
fields.label: Participant Type

fields.description: Where this participant is also somebody this farm invoices, the ERPNext Customer record. Optional, and the link is what stops the sales ledger and the competitive picture being two separate opinions about the same company.
fields.label: Customer

fields.description: The plan this participant was assessed under. Assessments age; tying one to the plan it was made for is what says how old.
fields.label: Strategic Plan

fields.description: 'Sweet cherry packing', 'custom harvest', 'organic apple'. Free text — the segment somebody competes in is not a taxonomy.
fields.label: Industry Segment

fields.description: The region they operate in — 'The Dalles', 'Yakima Valley', 'Central WA'.
fields.label: Geography

fields.description: What they grow or handle, comma-separated. Deliberately text rather than a link table: half these entries are somebody's recollection, and a Link would refuse to store 'cherries, maybe pears'.
fields.label: Crops

fields.description: Where they sit in the segment. The four are the standard Kotler positions and are used here because they map onto how somebody is likely to RESPOND to a move, which is what a competitive record is for.
fields.label: Market Position

fields.description: Estimated share of the segment named above. An estimate of a private figure — see the doctype description.
fields.label: Market Share (%)

fields.description: What they hold that is hard to replicate — water rights, a packing line, a variety licence, a buyer relationship. One per line.
fields.label: Key Assets

fields.description: When they are weakest and why — 'succession, owner is 71', 'note matures 2027'. One per line. This is the field that turns a competitor record into a decision.
fields.label: Vulnerability Windows

name: Market Participant
